stem: Aarav must draw a line through point $P$ that is parallel to a given line $AB$.

parts.text: Which claim correctly describes the construction?

options.text: Keep the same angle relationship to $AB$ with a set square or matching right-angle creases so the new line through $P$ does not meet $AB$.
The given point $P$ is already the name of the parallel line, so no construction at $P$ is needed.
Drawing a line through $P$ is what creates the given line $AB$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A parallel through $P$ is made by copying the angle relationship to $AB$ so the new line never meets $AB$. Point $P$ alone is not the parallel line, and the new line does not create $AB$.

teacher.key_rationale: Equal corresponding angles (or matched right angles) keep the lines parallel. Treating P as the line swaps the task for a label. Saying the new line creates AB reverses the given-to-constructed direction.
